title: GTA6 Map Size Compared to Four Massive Rockstar Games Combined
description: Check out the latest GTA6 community discussion on Reddit. A fan used Yannis v16 to compare the upcoming map size with four previous Rockstar titles.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## The Massive Scale of GTA6 Explored by the Community

As anticipation continues to build for Rockstar Games' upcoming blockbuster, the global fan base is constantly finding new ways to visualize the sheer scale of the next installment. Recently on the r/GTA6 Reddit community, user /u/Hammarsbald shared an intriguing perspective using a tool called Yannis v16 to break down just how massive the new map is expected to be.

According to the community post, when you combine the map sizes of four legendary titles—Vice City, GTA 4's Liberty City, GTA 5's Los Santos, and Red Dead Redemption 2—the resulting area is reportedly still smaller than the projected scale of the upcoming map.

### Excitement Meets Caution Regarding Map Density

While the visual comparison highlights Rockstar's ambitious approach to open-world design, it also brings up common concerns shared by the community. As the original poster noted, there is a lingering hope that the northern part of the map will not feel as empty as it might currently appear in these fan-made or tool-generated overviews.

It is important to emphasize that all community-driven maps, size comparisons, and speculative breakdowns are based on unconfirmed tools and leaked estimates. They **do not represent official statements, data, or confirmations from Rockstar Games**. Therefore, players should take these size comparisons with a grain of salt until official trailers and details confirm the true density and layout of the game world.

## Editor's Take

Fan-made comparisons are always a fascinating way to pass the time while waiting for official news. While it's exciting to imagine a world larger than four previous Rockstar masterpieces combined, the real challenge for the developers lies in filling that vast space with meaningful content rather than empty terrain. Only time will tell if the final product strikes the right balance between scale and depth.
